title: What you have to do
description: Say what is necessary, and what ought to happen.

explanation.summary: Spanish has a compound infinitive: tener que, deber, poder, querer followed by a participle instead of a plain infinitive. It says what is necessary, what you should do, and what you are able to do.

sections.heading: The three that take a participle
sections.body: Tener que plus a participle is an obligation that comes from outside: tengo que trabajar, I have to work. Poder plus a participle is what you are able to do: no puedo ir, I cannot go, but puedo ir mañana. Querer plus a participle is what you want to do: quiero ir, I want to go.

examples.es: Tengo que trabajar hasta las seis.
examples.en: I have to work until six.
I want to go, but I cannot.

sections.heading: Haber que, and who it is for
sections.body: Haber que is like tener que, but it says everybody has to: hay que esperar, we have to wait. And deber plus a plain infinitive says what you ought to do: debo llamar, I should call. The difference between deber and tener que is who says so: deber is your own judgement, tener que is a rule.

examples.es: Hay que pagar antes de entrar.
examples.en: You have to pay before going in.
